rationale: The financing leg is byte-identical to the archived "Capex-Peak Equity Cash Use" and "Post-Capex Equity Cash-Use Rescue," and the investment leg is simply a SUMRANK blend of those two signals' investment legs, making this an averaging variant of prior results rather than a new mechanism.

It is a recombination of archived ingredients (lagged investment leg × cash-consumed external financing), but lagging the replacement-burden measure genuinely removes contemporaneous sources-and-uses mechanical overlap and tests a distinct "weak conversion then rescue funding" sequence, so it is worth one test despite high overlap with Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing.

The prefunded-then-deployed sequencing is economically coherent and distinct from the contemporaneous "Equity-Funded Replacement Burden," though the MIN(net external, Δcash) stockpile leg has already produced weak, imprecise evidence twice in the archive, tempering the prior.

Internally consistent and a defensible pairing of an inventory-acceleration event with broad cash-consumed issuance, but it is the third crossing of the same lagged-ACCEL(invt) leg with a financing leg, and the two prior versions delivered strong FMB t-stats with economically trivial alphas — a diagnosis this proposal does not address.

Narrowing the archived "Post-Deal External Rescue" to its equity component is a substantive decomposition motivated by the pattern that equity-only financing legs delivered the larger alphas, and the overpayment/dilution story is coherent, though it remains a single-leg swap on an already-tested signal.

This keeps the exact investment leg of the archive's best performer ("Equity-Funded Replacement Burden," alpha -0.044, t -4.58) and merely substitutes a financing leg already used in "Equity-Timed Investment Peak," so it is a mechanical cross of two tested components with no new economic content and a likely weaker cash-use conditioning.
